groups.description: Who you talk to: personalities, voices, avatars and who may see them.
groups.label: Characters

groups.description: The models and servers DisPatch talks to, and how it finds them.
groups.label: Connections

groups.description: Speech recognition and voices (provided by the voice add-on).
groups.label: Voice

groups.description: Plugins, agent runtimes and the optional panes.
groups.label: Tools & Modules

groups.description: Sign-in, session lengths, and what programs holding the API key may do.
groups.label: People & Profiles

groups.description: Defaults for a new device: theme, language and avatar style.
groups.label: Appearance

retired.characters.default_audience: 4.0: who uses a character is each profile's household list (People), not an audience

settings.description: The address other devices use to reach DisPatch, e.g. https://chat.example.net. An https:// address tells the Health tab the connection is encrypted.
settings.label: Public address

settings.description: Say so when TLS ends at a proxy in front of DisPatch (Caddy, Tailscale Serve) so Health does not warn about plain HTTP.
settings.label: A reverse proxy provides HTTPS

settings.description: Local only (this computer), or your home network. The listen address itself is set by the launcher (--host, or BIND_ADDR in the Docker compose file); this records the decision so Health can tell you when the two disagree.
settings.label: Who can reach DisPatch

settings.description: What DisPatch reports as its own address. The launcher flag (--host) is what binds the port.
settings.label: Listen address (informational)

settings.description: The port DisPatch reports. The launcher flag (--port) is what binds it.
settings.label: Port (informational)

settings.description: How often the database is copied aside automatically (every 6 hours by default). Off turns it off.
settings.label: Database snapshot interval

settings.description: How many rotated database snapshots to keep before the oldest is deleted.
settings.label: Snapshots to keep

settings.description: Write a complete, encrypted backup (chats, characters, settings, avatars) on a schedule. The first one generates a recovery key and shows it once - keep it somewhere safe.
settings.label: Scheduled encrypted backups

settings.description: How often a scheduled encrypted backup is written.
settings.label: Encrypted backup interval

settings.description: Older encrypted backups are deleted beyond this many.
settings.label: Encrypted backups to keep

settings.description: Add the media and File Server folders to encrypted backups. They can be large.
settings.label: Include pictures and files

settings.description: The passphrase that encrypts backups. Leave empty to let DisPatch generate a recovery key. Either way it is kept in this install's secret store (the schedule needs it) and never shown again, so keep your own copy somewhere else.
settings.label: Backup passphrase

settings.description: Where the Health tab reads log lines from. Empty uses <data folder>/logs/dispatch.log.
settings.label: Log file

settings.description: How much the File Server may hold before uploads are refused (20 GB by default).
settings.label: File Server size limit

settings.description: Run the daily housekeeping (prune old log rows, tidy files, compact the database).
settings.label: Daily maintenance

settings.description: Local time of day (HH:MM) the housekeeping runs. It waits while a backup or an operator maintenance window is in progress.
settings.label: Daily maintenance time

settings.description: Forever (no cleanup) or only the last N months. Applies to every generated picture: reaction pictures already shown, Image Studio results, pictures made in chats and spent avatar-pool pictures. Pictures still in use are never removed; an expired picture is held in the trash before it is deleted.
settings.label: Generated images: keep

settings.description: Used when images are kept for N months. A picture counts as old when its last use in a chat and its own date are both older than this.
settings.label: Generated images: months to keep

settings.description: How long an expired picture stays recoverable before it is deleted for good.
settings.label: Expired images: days in the trash

settings.description: Sign-in and usage rows older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Activity log: days to keep

settings.description: Admin audit rows (who changed what) older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Audit log: days to keep

settings.description: Event logs of finished agent tasks older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Agent task events: days to keep

settings.description: Event rows of closed Job Board jobs older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Job events: days to keep

settings.description: Machine upload counters older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Daily usage counters: days to keep

settings.description: Records of already-mirrored agent transcript items older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Mirror de-duplication rows: days to keep

settings.description: Finished, failed and cancelled picture requests older than this are deleted (the picture itself follows the image rule above).
settings.label: Finished image jobs: days to keep

settings.description: Per-day agent usage totals older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Agent spend rows: days to keep

settings.description: Agent approval requests that have been decided, older than this, are deleted.
settings.label: Decided approvals: days to keep

settings.description: Votes and comments on closed Job Board jobs older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Closed-job feedback: days to keep

settings.description: A picture, avatar or upload that nothing refers to is moved to the trash only after this many days.
settings.label: Unreferenced files: grace days

settings.description: How long a swept file stays in the trash before it is deleted for good.
settings.label: Unreferenced files: days in the trash

settings.description: How many of the newest (6-hourly) database snapshots to keep.
settings.label: Database snapshots: recent to keep

settings.description: How many daily snapshots (the last one of each day) to keep beyond the recent ones.
settings.label: Database snapshots: daily to keep

settings.description: How many weekly snapshots (the last one of each week) to keep beyond the daily ones.
settings.label: Database snapshots: weekly to keep

settings.description: A mailto: address push services can reach if your server misbehaves. Empty uses a placeholder.
settings.label: Push notification contact

settings.description: How long an Admin session may sit idle before it locks.
settings.label: Admin auto-lock

settings.description: How long a User profile's session may sit idle before it ends.
settings.label: User session length

settings.description: How long a Basic profile's session may sit idle before it ends.
settings.label: Basic session length

settings.description: Where a lock and a device that has not signed in land: the default profile (shared by everyone who uses it) or the profile list.
settings.label: When locked, show

settings.description: The profile id a lock lands on when 'When locked, show' is the default profile. It must not be an Admin; agents and voice cloning are always off for it.
settings.label: Default profile

settings.description: Off, or how many days a device that ticks 'keep this device signed in' at sign-in stays signed in (renewed by use). Turning it off forgets every remembered device.
settings.label: Remember signed-in devices

settings.description: Let programs running on the same computer (agents, cron jobs) call the API without a key. Turn off once every program uses the machine API key.
settings.label: Trust programs on this computer

settings.description: How much programs holding the API key (agents, cron jobs) may upload through /api/upload per day, all together, so a looping agent cannot fill the disk. People have no daily limit.
settings.label: Machine uploads per day

settings.description: Show a short canned greeting at the top of a new chat (no model call is made).
settings.label: Greet new chats

settings.description: Connections to link-local and cloud-metadata addresses (169.254.x.x, fe80::, metadata.google.internal) are refused to stop DisPatch being used to reach internal services. Turn on only if you really run a model server there.
settings.label: Allow link-local and metadata targets

settings.description: The hosts Find servers probes for StudioForge, LM Studio, Ollama and OpenAI-style servers, on ports 1234, 8080 and 11434 (write host:port to probe one port). The default is this computer and the compose names studioforge, lmstudio and ollama (a name that does not resolve is skipped). Cloud-metadata and link-local addresses are never probed. host.docker.internal is added only inside a container; see the next setting.
settings.label: Find servers: where to look

settings.description: Inside a container, Find servers also probes host.docker.internal (ports 1234, 8080, 11434), which is the computer the container runs on. Turn off to stop that. It never happens outside a container, whatever this says.
settings.label: Find servers: look on the Docker host

settings.description: The connection a new character uses when you do not pick one.
settings.label: Default connection

settings.description: An MCP image server (ClawForge or compatible) for picture jobs, e.g. http://host:8700/mcp.
settings.label: Image server (MCP) address

settings.description: Where finished pictures are fetched from. Empty uses /files/ beside the MCP address.
settings.label: Image server file address

settings.description: DisPatch's own address as the image server sees it, so it can report a finished picture straight away instead of waiting to be asked.
settings.label: Callback address for the image server

settings.description: Let characters ask for pictures. Automatic turns it on when an image server or image API is configured.
settings.label: Picture jobs

settings.description: A command that makes one picture for the avatar and reaction pools. Empty turns the pools' automatic top-up off.
settings.label: Image command for picture pools

settings.description: How long to wait for one picture from the image command.
settings.label: Image command timeout

settings.description: A command that reports free GPU memory, so pools stay off a busy card.
settings.label: GPU status command

settings.description: A lease service the picture pools ask before using a shared GPU.
settings.label: GPU lease address

settings.description: Show StudioForge's control panel as a tool in the left rail. Needs the panel address below.
settings.label: StudioForge panel tab

settings.description: Where StudioForge's panel is, e.g. http://192.0.2.20:8080.
settings.label: StudioForge panel address

settings.description: The address a phone or laptop elsewhere can open (e.g. a Tailscale Serve HTTPS address).
settings.label: StudioForge panel address for other devices

settings.description: Web search, weather, Wikipedia, exchange rates and a calculator for direct-API characters. Off removes them from every character at once.
settings.label: Built-in lookups

settings.description: The openclaw program used for agent characters. Change it when it is not on the PATH.
settings.label: OpenClaw command

settings.description: How long an agent may take to answer before the turn is abandoned.
settings.label: Agent turn timeout

settings.description: How many agent turns may run at the same time (protects local models).
settings.label: Agents running at once

settings.description: Off: replies are read from transcripts. Shadow: connect and compare without delivering. On: replies arrive over the gateway socket.
settings.label: Agent gateway socket

settings.description: Automatic uses the gateway socket when connected, else the command line. Gateway only fails a turn rather than falling back; Command line always spawns the agent.
settings.label: How turns reach the agent

settings.description: Copy the agent runtime's own conversations into DisPatch threads.
settings.label: Mirror gateway chats

settings.description: How often the mirror checks while busy.
settings.label: Mirror check interval

settings.description: The longest the mirror waits between checks when nothing is happening.
settings.label: Mirror idle interval

settings.description: Conversations idle for longer than this when first seen are followed from now, not imported.
settings.label: Mirror history window

settings.description: Comma-separated session kinds to mirror (webchat, main, other).
settings.label: Mirror these session kinds

settings.description: A coding-agent pane (needs the dsh program). Automatic turns it on when dsh is installed.
settings.label: DeepSeek Harness pane

settings.description: The systemd user unit that runs dsh web.
settings.label: Harness service name

settings.description: The loopback port dsh web listens on.
settings.label: Harness port

settings.description: An address a browser elsewhere can open for the harness page.
settings.label: Harness address for other devices

settings.description: Show MailForge's dashboard as a tool. Automatic turns it on when MailForge's runtime files are found.
settings.label: Emails pane (MailForge)

settings.description: Where MailForge keeps its runtime files. Empty uses ~/.local/share/mailforge.
settings.label: MailForge data folder

settings.description: The address a browser elsewhere can open for MailForge.
settings.label: MailForge address for other devices

settings.description: A client-pipeline dashboard proxied from another service on this computer. Automatic turns it on when its PIN file exists.
settings.label: Clients pane

settings.description: Where the client-pipeline service listens.
settings.label: Clients service address

settings.description: A file holding the service's PIN. Empty uses ~/practice/keys/gui-pin.
settings.label: Clients service PIN file

settings.description: The theme a device uses until its user picks another.
settings.label: Default theme

settings.description: The language a device uses until its user picks another.
settings.label: Default language

settings.description: Rich shows full pictures, Minimal shows small round avatars. A device can override it.
settings.label: Default avatar style
